title: Count the Atoms of a Formula

concept.title: A new counting table for every parenthesis
body: A chemical formula such as `K4(ON(SO3)2)2` has element names (an uppercase letter and optionally lowercase letters: `Mg`, `O`), counts after an element, and **groups in parentheses** that are repeated by a count after `)`. The total count of every element is needed. A group in parentheses is like a small formula of its own whose counts must be **multiplied** by the number after `)` and added to the surrounding formula. A stack of tables is the natural tool.

Keep a **stack of maps** (element to count) and start with one empty map. On `(` push a new empty map. On `)` read the multiplier (1 if there is no number), pop the map on top, multiply every count in it, and add the result into the map that is now on top. On an element name read the count after it (1 if none) and add it to the map on top.

body.code:
stack = [{}]
"(":  stack.append({})
")":  mult = number after ")" or 1
       top = stack.pop()
       for name, c in top.items(): stack[-1][name] += c * mult
name: count = number after the name or 1;  stack[-1][name] += count

body: At the end the bottom map has the answer. Print the elements **sorted by name**; a count of 1 is not printed: `K4N2O14S4`. Sorting is the ordinary comparison of strings (`C` comes before `Ca`).

statement: A chemical formula is made of element names (an uppercase letter followed by any number of lowercase letters), counts (a number directly after an element or after a `)`; a missing number means 1) and groups in parentheses, which may be nested. Count how many atoms of each element the formula has. Print the elements sorted by name (the usual comparison of strings); after each name print its count, but only if the count is more than 1, with no separators.
inputFormat: One line with the formula (no spaces). It is always valid.
outputFormat: Print the result as one word, for example `K4N2O14S4`.
constraints: Every number in the formula is at most 1000.
Every count in the answer is at most 10^15.

examples.note: K: 4. Inside the group: O 1, N 1, S 2, O 6; times 2 gives O 14, N 2, S 4. Sorted: K4N2O14S4.

hints: Treat each parenthesis as a new table of counts, kept on a stack.
At `)` multiply the table on top by the number that follows and merge it into the table below.
Sort the names before printing, and skip the number when the count is 1.

explanation: A stack of maps holds one table of counts per open parenthesis. At `)` the top table is multiplied by the number after it and merged into the table below; the sorted bottom table is printed.
solution.complexity: Time O(n * k) for k different elements, space O(n).

code.python:
s = input().strip()

stack = [{}]
i = 0
n = len(s)
while i < n:
    ch = s[i]
    if ch == "(":
        stack.append({})
        i += 1
    elif ch == ")":
        i += 1
        j = i
        while j < n and s[j].isdigit():
            j += 1
        mult = int(s[i:j]) if j > i else 1
        i = j
        top = stack.pop()
        for name, c in top.items():
            stack[-1][name] = stack[-1].get(name, 0) + c * mult
    else:
        j = i + 1
        while j < n and s[j].islower():
            j += 1
        name = s[i:j]
        i = j
        while j < n and s[j].isdigit():
            j += 1
        count = int(s[i:j]) if j > i else 1
        i = j
        stack[-1][name] = stack[-1].get(name, 0) + count
print("".join(name + (str(c) if c > 1 else "") for name, c in sorted(stack[0].items())))
